content_units: Dinner Party Playlist Vibe

Warm, polished, and easy to talk over—this 90-minute sequence leans neo-soul, jazz-pop, light funk, and mellow electronic without turning the room into a dance floor. It starts inviting, settles into a richer mid-dinner groove, then softens into a sleek late-evening glide.
18-Track Dinner Flow
Section   Artist   Song   Mood
1   Opening   Sade   Kiss of Life   smooth, elegant
2   Opening   Norah Jones   Sunrise   cozy, conversational
3   Opening   Jordan Rakei   Eye to Eye   modern soul, relaxed
4   Opening   Emily King   Remind Me   warm, intimate
5   Opening   Tom Misch   Movie   breezy, refined
6   Opening   Corinne Bailey Rae   Like a Star   soft glow, welcoming
7   Peak Dinner   SAULT   Wildfires   restrained groove
8   Peak Dinner   Jungle   Lucky I Got What I Want   light funk, polished
9   Peak Dinner   Rhye   Open   lush, low-key sensual
10   Peak Dinner   Lianne La Havas   Green & Gold   soulful, buoyant
11   Peak Dinner   Moonchild   The List   jazzy, silky
12   Peak Dinner   Jessie Ware   Spotlight   sleek, controlled pulse
13   Peak Dinner   FKJ   Vibin' Out   instrumental-leaning, smooth
14   Wind-Down   KAYTRANADA feat. H.E.R.   Intimidated   mellow late-night groove
15   Wind-Down   The Cinematic Orchestra   To Build a Home   gentle, reflective
16   Wind-Down   Zero 7 feat. Sia   Destiny   airy, calm
17   Wind-Down   Air   All I Need   dreamy, understated
18   Wind-Down   Erykah Badu   Didn't Cha Know?   soft close, soulful
Hosting Notes for This Sequence
-   Opening:   tracks 1-6 ease people into the room without pulling focus from greetings and first drinks.
-   Peak dinner:   tracks 7-13 add texture and momentum while staying dinner-appropriate and conversation-friendly.
-   Wind-down:   tracks 14-18 lower the energy gradually for dessert, final pours, and lingering conversation.
Approximate total playtime:   88-96 minutes  , depending on version/album edits on your streaming service.
Quick Adjustments
- If you want it   slightly more jazzy  , swap in Melody Gardot or Diana Krall for one of the mid-set tracks.
- If you want it   more modern and electronic  , replace one opening song with Bonobo or Roosevelt.
- If you want it   safer and even less lyrical  , swap one or two vocal tracks for instrumental FKJ, Khruangbin, or BadBadNotGood cuts.
